subject.title: after_tool_call hook receives a flattened string, not the structured ToolResult — plugins cannot detect exec/bash failures

question: Should OpenClaw canonicalize Codex-native shell/apply_patch `after_tool_call` payloads from app-server completion data instead of forwarding Codex's raw string `PostToolUse` response as the plugin-visible result?
rationale: The bug is source-proven, but the repair changes a public plugin hook payload/timing boundary and must choose between native-relay immediacy, app-server structured fidelity, duplicate-event suppression, and raw-string compatibility.

options.title: Canonical structured OpenClaw payload
options.body: Use app-server commandExecution/file-change completion data as the plugin-visible `after_tool_call` result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress the raw string relay for those tools.

options.title: Wait for upstream Codex payloads
options.body: Keep OpenClaw relay behavior stable and require Codex to emit structured shell/apply_patch `tool_response` data before changing the plugin contract.

options.title: Document raw-string behavior
options.body: Treat Codex `PostToolUse` strings as the intended compatibility contract and direct plugins to another surface for exit-code observability.

recommendation.title: Canonical structured OpenClaw payload
recommendation.body: Use app-server commandExecution/file-change completion data as the plugin-visible `after_tool_call` result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress the raw string relay for those tools.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public plugin hook/tool-result API boundary decision that follows the middleware scope introduced in PR 71021.
